evidence: host/native/checkpoint.lisp:143-153: `(fnn-log-history-each store (lambda (record) (let ((octets (fnn-octet-list record))) ... (let ((event (fnn-core 'fn-store-log-reclaim-event octets ctx))) ... (push (fnn-octets event) rewritten))))))`, then :180-187 `(let ((history (nreverse rewritten))) ... (fnn-recover-log-replay store history (fnn-config-records store))`. books/store-log-reclaim.lisp:62-68 advertises this path as `The streamed decision (what the host calls; D27 ...) ... No list of the history is ever built in ACL2.`
fix: Stream the rewrite instead of collecting it. Make two passes over the log: the first folds the decision (fn-rcls-step), and the second re-reads each record, rewrites it (fn-rclp-event) and feeds it straight into the chunked replay (fnn-recover-log-stream-take/-flush, as the open's full replay already does). The ACL2 decision is a pure function of the record and ctx, so the second pass produces exactly the same rewritten history.
reviewer: In checkpoint.lisp:143-153 every record goes through fnn-octet-list (an ACL2 octet list per record) and its rewrite is pushed as an octet vector onto `rewritten`. At :180-187 the whole list is nreversed and handed to fnn-recover-log-replay. Heap use therefore grows with the whole history. store-log-reclaim.lisp:62-68 only claims that no list is built inside ACL2, and the host's list is real. resource-contract.md:752-754 lists compaction's memory as unbounded (PKT-842) but does not name reclaim. This is an offline verb only, so the served path is not affected.
scenario: Take a store whose log holds 200 GB of article records, of which 1% are reclaimable. `operator CONFIG store reclaim` pushes an octet vector for every record, and every live article payload is in that set, so the process needs about 200 GB of heap before the replay begins. On top of that, each record is first expanded to an ACL2 octet list (about 16 bytes per octet) while it is rewritten. The verb is OOM-killed, or the box swap-thrashes, and the store's released payloads can never be reclaimed offline. The work and allocation scale with the whole store, not with the step, which violates D27's 'bound work and allocation per scheduling step'.
title: Offline `store reclaim` keeps the entire rewritten history in memory before replaying it
